items.prompt: In a partner webhook delivery system, an integration service must deliver a status change. the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates The design review focuses on ordering, partitioning, replay, and consumer position. The normal path is healthy and the design must show where the decision belongs. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is partition and track consumer position according to the scope of ordering and replay that users require..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Partition and track consumer position according to the scope of ordering and replay that users require. In this normal path for partner webhook delivery, ordering is usually local to a key or partition; replay needs durable history and explicit cursor ownership. The owner must also make a receiver that acknowledges late observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide ordering, partitioning, replay, and consumer position independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a receiver that acknowledges late as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Partition and track consumer position according to the scope of ordering and replay that users require. It addresses the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates through an explicit mechanism and keeps a receiver that acknowledges late inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Ordering is usually local to a key or partition; replay needs durable history and explicit cursor ownership. The applicability case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For partner webhook delivery, the decision keeps the receiver may retry and may observe duplicates attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a receiver that acknowledges late as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Ordering, partitioning, replay, and consumer position” to terminology recall. Messaging products are not interchangeable; distinguish transient commands, durable work, event notification, replayable history, and workflow state. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce ordering, partitioning, replay, and consumer position must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to Apache Kafka design documentation (https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#design); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.

items.prompt: In a telemetry ingestion system, an observability collector must accept device measurements. bursty producers must not make the query path unavailable The design review focuses on ordering, partitioning, replay, and consumer position. The same mechanism appears in a different domain with one constraint changed. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: bursty producers must not make the query path unavailable
Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
The primary decision is partition and track consumer position according to the scope of ordering and replay that users require..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Partition and track consumer position according to the scope of ordering and replay that users require. In this transfer case for telemetry ingestion, ordering is usually local to a key or partition; replay needs durable history and explicit cursor ownership. The owner must also make a producer burst exceeding consumer capacity observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide ordering, partitioning, replay, and consumer position independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a producer burst exceeding consumer capacity as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Partition and track consumer position according to the scope of ordering and replay that users require. It addresses bursty producers must not make the query path unavailable through an explicit mechanism and keeps a producer burst exceeding consumer capacity inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Ordering is usually local to a key or partition; replay needs durable history and explicit cursor ownership. The transfer case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For telemetry ingestion, the decision keeps bursty producers must not make the query path unavailable attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a producer burst exceeding consumer capacity as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Ordering, partitioning, replay, and consumer position” to terminology recall. Messaging products are not interchangeable; distinguish transient commands, durable work, event notification, replayable history, and workflow state. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce ordering, partitioning, replay, and consumer position must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to Apache Kafka design documentation (https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#design); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.
